changes.description: Model the `look at <object> under the <light>` goal family (the third ALFWorld task type, previously unmodelled) in GoalPlannerMiddleware. _parse_goal gained a branch that recognises `look at <obj> ... under|with|in|near <tool>` and maps it onto the existing examine mode (target = object, dest = lamp/tool kind); before this it fell through to the placement branch with an empty destination, so `look at pen under the desklamp` was planned as `put pen in/on <whatever>` and declared `goal complete` the moment the pen had been dropped - while the observation offered `use desklamp 1`, the only action that can satisfy a light goal. _plan_examine now drives the real sequence: (1) take the goal object (or walk back to where it was seen), (2) walk to the surface that offers `use <lamp>` - remembered per-episode in the new light_places map, ordered by the new LIGHT_PRIOR list when the lamp is still unseen, (3) `use` the lamp exactly once (lamp = toggle; light_on flag, so a second `use` that would switch it back off is never emitted), (4) `examine` the goal object, and (5) only if the episode has not ended, leave the object on the lamp's surface via the new _put_on guard (light_put flag stops the planner from walking back and re-taking it), which also covers the literal 'object under the lamp' reading. The [PLAN] header for this family now reports `desklamp=on|off` instead of a meaningless `placed=0/1`, and the examine-mode override now enforces the take / `use <lamp>` / walk-to-lamp / examine / place-under-lamp steps and refuses to `put` the goal object down before the light is on or to take any object that is not the goal object (e.g. the lamp itself).
changes.failure_pattern: Goal-family misparse: an `examine/look-at-in-light` goal is planned as a placement goal with an empty destination, so the planner reports a false 'goal complete' after the first drop and never recommends the offered `use <lamp>` action; the episode then wastes the whole 50-action budget in a fake done state (iteration-5 task native_58763bce..., goal 'look at pen under the desklamp', 50 actions, reward 0).
predicted_fixes: every future episode whose goal line is `look at the <object> under the <light>` (ALFWorld look_at_obj_in_light, the family the iteration-3 analysis recorded as 'completely unmodelled' and the iteration-3 goal-parser test only checked did not break: 'look at the alarmclock under the desklamp')

episodes phrased `examine the <object> with the <lamp>` (same task type, same `use <lamp>` action): the walk-to-lamp, use-once and place-under-lamp steps are now planned instead of only `use` when the agent happens to already stand at the lamp
risk_tasks: examine/light tasks whose tool is not on a lamp-carrying surface or is inside a closed container: the lamp search is ordered by LIGHT_PRIOR and only falls back to the general sweep, costing a few extra actions

examine/light tasks where the environment ends the episode only on `use`: the extra `examine`/placement step is never reached because the harness stops on the winning action (verified: the winning action is the last message of every passing iteration-5 trace)

examine/light tasks where the goal object must be dropped somewhere other than the lamp's surface: the hedge placement is only ever issued after `use` and `examine` failed to end the episode, i.e. in states that were losses before
changes.why_this_component: The goal line is parsed and the next action is chosen by the middleware, whose [PLAN] block is what the traces show the model following (in the failing episode every action was exactly the planner's recommendation, including the wrong `put pen 1 in/on desk 1`). The advisory text alone cannot work here: the system prompt/skill/memory already described `examine X with Y`, yet the model had no way to know that `use desklamp 1` was the relevant action and that the goal was not a placement - and the middleware's false 'goal complete' statement actively misled it. Only the middleware holds the per-episode state (available actions, place, carried, seen objects, lamp place) needed to sequence take -> use -> examine.

changes.description: Advisory text kept in sync with chg-15 (text only): systemprompt.md goal family 4 now covers both phrasings (`examine the <object> with the <tool>` and `look at the <object> under the <light>`), states that the object must be in hand at the tool, that the switch is the `use <tool>` action offered only while standing at the surface that carries the lamp, that a lamp is a toggle so it must be used exactly once, and that the object must never be put down elsewhere; skills/alfworld_playbook.md gets the same rule in the goal-family list; LongTermMEMORY.md pitfall 12 is extended from `examine X with Y` to the `look at X under Y` wording with the same use-once / never-put rule; tool_descriptions/take_action.tool.yaml (description only) gains one sentence saying that for these goals the winning action is `use <lamp>` while holding the object next to the lamp, and that putting the object down elsewhere is wrong unless the [PLAN] line names the lamp's surface.
changes.failure_pattern: Knowledge gap for the light goal family: no advisory text anywhere described `look at X under Y`, and the existing `examine X with Y` bullet did not say that the switch is `use <lamp>` or that the lamp is a toggle, so a model that ignores the [PLAN] block has no grounded rule for this family.
predicted_fixes: future `look at / examine ... <lamp>` episodes where the model reasons from the prompt instead of the [PLAN] block
risk_tasks: none identified - the added text is scoped to the light family and restates the existing placement rules for every other goal
changes.why_this_component: The frozen text files are the only carrier for rules that should hold even when the model's own reasoning overrides the [PLAN] block, and the tool description is read at the moment the action is written. Text alone was insufficient before (the family was unmodelled in code), so it is applied as a complement to chg-15, not as the fix.

changes.description: Hardening follow-up to chg-15, found by the stub-environment tests: (a) the planner no longer suppresses the examine step after a *pre-lamp* examine - a new per-episode flag `examined_lit` is set only when the goal object is examined while the lamp is already on and held, so an early `examine <object>` (which the model may issue before reaching the lamp and which cannot satisfy a light goal) never costs the real examine in the light; (b) the examine-mode override now also replaces an `examine <carried goal object>` issued before the lamp is on when the plan is a `go to` step, so a model that wants to inspect the object on the spot is put back on the planned walk toward the lamp instead of looping on the same examine.
changes.failure_pattern: Two ways a light-goal episode can still stall after chg-15: the examine-in-the-light step is skipped because the object was already examined elsewhere (losing the `examine` win condition), or the model repeats a useless `examine` of the object before the lamp is on instead of walking to the lamp.
predicted_fixes: future `look at / examine ... <lamp>` episodes where the model inspects the object before switching the light on
risk_tasks: none identified - both rules live inside the light family and only replace an action that cannot win the goal with the planned step
changes.why_this_component: Same enforcement point as chg-15: only the middleware knows whether the lamp is on, which object is carried and where the lamp was offered, so only it can order the actions reliably; the stub-environment tests showed the prompt-side rule alone cannot prevent the premature examine.

rollback_decision.chg-11: KEEP - verdict 'INEFFECTIVE' in the auto-report is not sound: its predicted tasks were infrastructure exceptions in this run, so the change was never measured; the cost-aware search order is consistent with the current behaviour of all 9 non-look-at released traces, so rolling it back would be evidence-free.
rollback_decision.chg-12: KEEP - same reason (predicted task not measured; no regression evidence).
rollback_decision.chg-13: KEEP - same reason; additionally the seen-object recall is what makes the new light plan able to find the goal object cheaply, and the nine non-look-at replays are unchanged.
rollback_decision.chg-14: KEEP - text kept in sync with chg-11/12/13; no evidence of harm (48/50 tasks passed).
